summary: Remote WebSocket server granted interactive shell control of installer host via PTY write path
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent runs a long-lived agent that connects to a configurable WebSocket server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via SERVER_URL / config) and dispatches server-sent messages into privileged local operations. The `terminal_input` handler writes `msg.data` directly into a spawned PTY (bash/powershell/cmd via node-pty), giving whatever server the agent is pointed at full interactive shell control of the host running the agent. Additional server-driven handlers expose remote file read/write, git operations against local repos, and an `upgrade_agent` action that shells out to `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` and spawns a detached bash/VBScript wrapper to swap files and restart the systemd/launchd/PM2 service. service/linux.js also mutates PATH to prepend `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` for the agent's execution environment. The self-upgrade fetches from the official npm registry at the vendor's own package name, so the source of upgrade bytes is pinned to the publisher, but the trigger is remote-controlled. The remote-controlled shell path fires only when a user explicitly runs the agent CLI (not on `npm install` or on `require()`), and the destination server is operator-configured; nonetheless the shape is a network-driven PTY with no in-band authentication/authorization visible in the handler, so any party controlling the configured WebSocket endpoint has interactive host control.
